title: Prove: Bottom-up heapify is linear
body:
Constructing a binary heap by calling sift-down from the last internal node to the root takes O(n) time.

Complexity: O(n) time and O(1) extra space, versus O(n log n) for repeated insertion.

title: Invariant: Bottom-up heapify is linear
body: Before node i is processed, every subtree rooted at an index greater than i is already a valid heap.

title: Proof step: Leaves are heaps
body: Nodes with no children already satisfy the heap property, so processing can start at the last parent.

title: Proof step: Process internal nodes bottom-up
body:
Walking from the last parent down to the root guarantees each child subtree is a heap before its parent is fixed.

Depends on: leaves

title: Proof step: Cost depends on height
body:
A node at height h moves at most h levels, and a binary heap has at most ceil(n / 2^(h+1)) nodes at height h.

Depends on: reverse

title: Proof step: Bound the weighted sum
body:
The sum over heights of h * n / 2^(h+1) is at most n, because the series sum h / 2^h converges to 2.

Depends on: height-cost
